arxiv-2108-01804.title: Online Training of Spiking Recurrent Neural Networks with Phase-Change Memory Synapses
arxiv-2108-01804.creator: Yiğit Demirağ, Charlotte Frenkel, Melika Payvand, Giacomo Indiveri
arxiv-2108-01804.description: Abstract Spiking RNN are a promising tool for solving a wide variety of complex cognitive and motor tasks, due to their rich temporal dynamics and sparse processing. However training spiking RNN on dedicated neuromorphic hardware is still an open challenge.

arxiv-2109-08095.title: Influence of Heliolatitudinal Anisotropy of Solar FUV/EUV Emissions on Lyman- α \alpha Helioglow: SOHO/SWAN Observations and WawHelioGlow Modeling Journal: ApJL scikit-learn ( Pedregosa et al. 2011 ) , astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 )
arxiv-2109-08095.creator: M. Strumik, M. Bzowski, M. A. Kubiak
arxiv-2109-08095.description: Abstract Observations of the Sun’s surface suggest a nonuniform radiated flux as related to the presence of bright active regions and darker coronal holes. The variations of the FUV/EUV source radiation can be expected to affect the Lyman- α \alpha backscatter glow measured by spaceborne instruments.

arxiv-2111-04669.title: Software mitigation of coherent two-qubit gate errors
arxiv-2111-04669.creator: Lingling Lao, Alexander Korotkov, Zhang Jiang, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Thomas E. O’Brien, Dan E. Browne
arxiv-2111-04669.description: Abstract Two-qubit gates are important components of quantum computing. However, unwanted interactions between qubits (so-called parasitic gates) can be particularly problematic and degrade the performance of quantum applications. In this work, we present two software methods to mitigate parasitic two-qubit gate errors.

arxiv-2303-16971.title: Sparse joint shift in multinomial classification
arxiv-2303-16971.description: Abstract . Sparse joint shift (SJS) was recently proposed as a tractable model for general dataset shift which may cause changes to the marginal distributions of features and labels as well as the posterior probabilities and the class-conditional feature distributions.

arxiv-2402-16090.title: Key Design Choices in Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation: An In-depth Empirical Analysis
arxiv-2402-16090.creator: Andrea Maracani, Raffaello Camoriano, Elisa Maiettini, Davide Talon, Lorenzo Rosasco, Lorenzo Natale
arxiv-2402-16090.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Andrea Maracani, Raffaello Camoriano, Elisa Maiettini, Davide Talon, Lorenzo Rosasco, Lorenzo Natale. This study provides a comprehensive benchmark framework for Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (SF-UDA) in image classification, aiming to achieve a rigorous empirical understanding of the complex relationships between multiple key design factors in SF-UDA methods. The study empirically examines a diverse set of SF-UDA techniques, assessing their consistency across datasets, sensitivity to specific hyperparameters, and applicability across different families of backbone architectures.

arxiv-2406-06491.title: Input Driven Synchronization of Chaotic Neural Networks with Analyticaly Determined Conditional Lyapunov Exponents
arxiv-2406-06491.creator: Jordan Culp, Wilten Nicola
arxiv-2406-06491.description: Abstract Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with random, but sufficiently strong and balanced coupling display a well known high-dimensional chaotic dynamics. Here, we investigate if externally applied inputs to these RNNs can stabilize globally synchronous, input-dependent solutions, in spite of the strong chaos-inducing coupling.

arxiv-2407-06630.title: Toychain: A Simple Blockchain for Research in Swarm Robotics
arxiv-2407-06630.creator: Alexandre Pacheco, Ulysse Denis, Raina Zakir, Volker Strobel, Andreagiovanni Reina, Marco Dorigo
arxiv-2407-06630.description: Abstract This technical report describes the implementation of Toychain: a simple, lightweight blockchain implemented in Python, designed for ease of deployment and practicality in robotics research. It can be integrated with various software and simulation tools used in robotics (we have integrated it with ARGoS, Gazebo, and ROS2), and also be deployed on real robots capable of Wi-Fi communications.

arxiv-2410-22265.title: NCA-Morph: Medical Image Registration with Neural Cellular Automata
arxiv-2410-22265.creator: Amin Ranem, John Kalkhof Anirban Mukhopadhyay
arxiv-2410-22265.description: Abstract Medical image registration is a critical process that aligns various patient scans, facilitating tasks like diagnosis, surgical planning, and tracking. Traditional optimization-based methods are slow, prompting the use of Deep Learning (DL) techniques, such as VoxelMorph and Transformer-based strategies, for faster results. However, these DL methods often impose significant resource demands.

arxiv-2505-16913.title: Quantum systems with jump-discontinous mass. I
arxiv-2505-16913.creator: Fabio Deelan Cunden, Giovanni Gramegna, Marilena Ligabò
arxiv-2505-16913.description: Abstract . We consider a free quantum particle in one dimension whose mass profile exhibits jump discontinuities. The corresponding Hamiltonian is realised as a self-adjoint extension of the kinetic energy operator formulated in divergence form, with the extension encoded in the boundary conditions at the mass discontinuity points.

arxiv-2605-16385.title: Hilbert-Geo: Solving Solid Geometric Problems by Neural-Symbolic Reasoning
arxiv-2605-16385.creator: Ruoran Xu, Haoyu Cheng, Bin Dong, Qiufeng Wang

pmc-10824989.title: Tour guide robot: a 5G-enabled robot museum guide
pmc-10824989.creator: Stefano Rosa, Marco Randazzo, Ettore Landini, Stefano Bernagozzi, Giancarlo Sacco, Mara Piccinino, Lorenzo Natale
pmc-10824989.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This paper presents and discusses the development and deployment of a tour guide robot as part of the 5 g-TOURS EU research project, aimed at developing applications enabled by 5G technology in different use cases. The objective is the development of an autonomous robotic application where intelligence is off-loaded to a remote machine via 5G network, so as to lift most of the computational load from the robot itself.

pmc-12625168.title: Population Pharmacokinetic Modeling and Pediatric Exposure of Dexamethasone Sodium Phosphate Encapsulated in Erythrocytes (eDSP) Administered Monthly for Treatment of Neurological Symptoms of Patients With Ataxia Telangiectasia
pmc-12625168.creator: Deniz Ozdin, Leila Kheibarshekan, Giovanni Mambrini, Pierre‐Olivier Tremblay
pmc-12625168.description: The EryDex System (EDS) is a drug/device combination, which has been tested in clinical trials for ataxia telangiectasia (AT). EDS encapsulates dexamethasone sodium phosphate (DSP) solution in autologous erythrocytes at the point of care, and encapsulated DSP (eDSP) is infused back into the patient. Low doses of dexamethasone are released from erythrocytes over a 30‐day period.

pmc-12693626.title: SAFARI: pangenome alignment of ancient DNA using purine/pyrimidine encodings
pmc-12693626.creator: Joshua Rubin, Jan van Waaij, Louis Kraft, Jouni Sirén, Peter Wad Sackett, Gabriel Renaud
pmc-12693626.description: Aligning DNA sequences retrieved from fossils or other paleontological artifacts, referred to as ancient DNA (aDNA), is particularly challenging due to the short sequence length and chemical damage which creates a specific pattern of substitution (CT and GA) in addition to the heightened divergence between the sample and the reference genome thus exacerbating reference bias.

pmc-13182088.title: Feed-forward neural networks for genomic selection: insights into varying levels of dominance heritability
pmc-13182088.creator: Hamid Sahebalam, Mohsen Gholizadeh
pmc-13182088.description: Genomic selection enables the prediction of genetic and breeding values from high-dimensional marker data, improving selection efficiency in breeding programs. Feed-forward neural networks (FFNN) are a type of deep learning model that approximates complex non-linear relationships between markers and traits through interconnected layers of neurons.

pmc-13333697.title: Athletic performance levels across biological maturity status in youth soccer players
pmc-13333697.creator: Giuseppe Scardina, Guglielmo Pillitteri, Domenico Savio Salvatore Vicari, Alberto Canzone, Filipe Manuel Clemente, Valerio Giustino, Antonino Bianco

pmc-13413917.title: A Narrative Review of Psychological and Physical Rehabilitation in Infertility Treatment: Toward Holistic Outcomes Beyond Conception
pmc-13413917.creator: Muhammad Adib Dwi Tamma Putra, Muhammad Ayub Endratamma, Muhammad Fadill Akbar, Adila A. Hamid, Mohd Helmy Mokhtar
pmc-13413917.description: Infertility is a complex health issue that extends beyond biological mechanisms, encompassing significant psychological, relational, and social aspects. Advances in assisted reproductive technologies have improved the chances of conception, yet many couples discontinue treatment due to stress, stigma, and reduced quality of life.

pmc-13450457.title: An umbrella review synthesising published systematic review evidence for self-harm and suicidality among patients diagnosed with an eating or feeding disorder
pmc-13450457.creator: Anoushka Baluja, Roger T Webb
pmc-13450457.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In recent years there has been a proliferation of systematic reviews on the association between feeding and eating disorders and self-harm and suicidality. This study aims to conduct an umbrella review, providing a top-level synthesis of this information. A systematic search was performed using two databases (MEDLINE and APA PsycInfo), with inclusion criteria of studies identifying as systemic reviews, written in English, and researching the association between feeding and eating disorders and self-harm and/or suicidality.

pmc-13451645.title: Preserving Valued Activities in Life for Adults With Rheumatoid Arthritis: Development and Pre‐Testing Refinement of the PREVAIL Model of Care
pmc-13451645.creator: Louise M. Thoma, Joel R. Thompson, Jason Sharpe, Beth Jonas, Patti Katz, Kelli Allen

pmc-13483941.title: Periodontal health in a longitudinal French cohort of people with Parkinson’s disease
pmc-13483941.creator: J Samot, E Courtin, D Guehl, N Damon-Perriere, O Branchard, M Saint-Jean, V Chuy, B Ella, M C Badet
pmc-13483941.description: Motor impairment associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD) can hinder daily oral hygiene. This study aimed to assess the microbiological and clinical evolution of periodontal health in people with PD. This prospective cohort study included participants with PD. Clinical oral health data and microbiological samples were collected at baseline and after a follow-up period (median 7 months [range: 3–21]).

pmc-13527162.title: Dynamic Global and Local Enhancement of Theta‐Band Functional Networks as Neural Markers of Spinal Cord Stimulation Efficacy in Disorders of Consciousness
pmc-13527162.creator: Yinuo Liu, Qianqian Ge, Jiewei Lu, Yaqian Li, Jianda Han, Jianghong He, Ningbo Yu
pmc-13527162.description: BackgroundSpinal cord stimulation (SCS) has emerged as a promising intervention for patients with disorders of consciousness (DoC). However, clinical optimization is hindered by a lack of interpretable prognostic biomarkers, and the neural mechanisms associated with recovery after SCS remain largely elusive.
